stories.headline: Democrats Win Congress; Republicans Split Over Blame for Losses
stories.dek: Trump and Vance tied the party's worst midterm losses in half a century to the Iran war and prices, while Democrats vow to focus on affordability and oversight.
pole_a_bullets: The loss traces to the Iran war's effect on oil prices, as Trump said, and does not reflect a rejection of conservative policy.
Midterms usually punish the sitting president's party. Trump said Republicans would have won had he been on the ballot.
A Democratic majority is not a blank check: Trump has signaled he will veto rollbacks of his agenda.
Voters were promised affordability. Republicans argue that investigations and impeachments would not deliver it.
pole_b_bullets: Voters rejected Trump's agenda, including in deep-red states, and that is a clear repudiation.
The message was to do more on affordability and corruption, and Jeffries has pledged to focus on cost of living.
Unified control lets Democrats investigate the administration and reject nominees. They argue the president has faced too few checks.
Trump's tariffs and the Iran war now face congressional scrutiny, and Trump and Vance have both acknowledged the war hurt the party.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions commonly voiced by Republican officials and conservative commentators.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions commonly voiced by Democratic leaders such as Hakeem Jeffries and liberal commentators.
evidence_left: NBC News projects Democrats will control both the House and Senate from January. Yahoo News reported Democrats flipped seven Senate seats to lead 54-44, with Mississippi still being counted.
CNN reported Democrats were projected to win over 250 House seats, ousting 30 GOP incumbents.
evidence_right: The Washington Post reported Trump and Vance both acknowledged the Iran war and its effect on prices contributed to the losses. MS NOW reported Vance asked on X whether the war was worth losing the majorities.
NBC News (citing four sources on a staff call) and The Washington Post (citing a top aide) reported House Speaker Mike Johnson will not stay on as GOP leader.
stories.sources_line: Sourced from NBC News, The Washington Post, MS NOW, Yahoo News, November 05, 2026.

stories.headline: Nasdaq Falls 5.5% Into Correction as AI Stocks Sell Off After Midterms
stories.dek: The Dow lost about 1,800 points a day after a post-election rally, as investors weighed possible limits on data center construction.
pole_a_bullets: The selloff is driven by policy fear, not earnings. AMD's CEO says demand outstrips supply and expects revenue growth above 80% in 2027.
No AI restrictions have been enacted. Trump has signaled vetoes, and Democrats are divided on a blanket freeze.
UBS puts about 30% of expected 2028 data center capacity additions at risk, which leaves most of the buildout intact.
Indexes remain up for the year, and some strategists, such as Jim Cramer, say the AI trade is not going away.
pole_b_bullets: Valuations had priced in perfection. One fund manager said the market is moving from the promise of AI to the price of AI.
The policy risk is real: Democrats hold Congress and gained governorships, and Texas holds an estimated 27% of planned U.S. data center capacity.
Credit stress is showing: CoreWeave's five-year default spreads hit a record, and The Hill reported AI-debt worries.
The damage is broad. The Russell 2000 also entered a correction, and the VIX surged the most since April.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions commonly voiced by market strategists and AI-sector executives.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions commonly voiced by valuation-focused fund managers and credit analysts.
evidence_left: CBS News and CNBC reported the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52% to close at 24,315, more than 10% below its October record. CNBC data showed the S&P 500 down 4.36% to 7,353.73.
Value lost differs by outlet: CNN reported $2.5 trillion wiped from the market; Reuters, via The Globe and Mail, reported $3 trillion lost from S&P 500 companies.
evidence_right: CNBC reported the Dow rose more than 1,500 points on Wednesday, its best day since April 2025. The Globe and Mail, citing Reuters, reported the S&P 500 was still up 7.4% for 2026 and the Nasdaq up 4.6% after Thursday.

Yahoo Finance reported AMD fell about 13% in morning trading despite a record quarter. Reuters, via Yahoo, reported UBS estimates about 30% of expected 2028 U.S. data center capacity additions could face construction pauses.
stories.sources_line: Sourced from CBS News, CNBC, Reuters via Yahoo Finance, The Globe and Mail, November 05, 2026.

stories.headline: Democrats Push to Curb AI Data Centers as OpenAI Offers Voluntary Pledges
stories.dek: After midterm wins, Sanders and others called for a national moratorium, and OpenAI published data center commitments two days after the vote.
pole_a_bullets: A national moratorium would only move demand overseas, since one analyst said location is fungible.
Targeted rules, such as paying full power costs and publishing plans, can address local concerns without a freeze.
Some Democrats warn a blanket freeze could hamper AI progress and undermine national security.
Investors and workers tied to the buildout already face losses on mere policy fear.
pole_b_bullets: Voters rejected data centers at the ballot. Sanders says communities want limits on harm to the environment, jobs and electricity bills.
Company pledges are voluntary and cover only data centers the company owns and operates.
OpenAI itself urged policymakers to turn its commitments into law, which supports binding rules.
Concentrated buildout, such as Texas's large share of planned capacity, makes state and federal oversight timely.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions commonly voiced by AI-industry analysts and moderate Democrats.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions commonly voiced by Sen. Bernie Sanders, Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and local anti-data-center campaigners.
evidence_left: Sanders posted "National data center moratorium now" on Nov. 4. He and Ocasio-Cortez had introduced an AI Data Center Moratorium Act earlier this year.

A CNBC voter poll, as summarized by Briefs Finance, found 56% saw AI and data centers as a key consideration and 65% of them chose a Democrat. Ballot-measure counts differ: Gate reported voters rejected 40 of 41 measures across 10 states, while Sanders cited 43 of 44 communities.
evidence_right: CNBC reported OpenAI published commitments Thursday to pay the full cost of data center power, solicit community input, and publish construction plans. Crypto Briefing noted they cover only company-owned and operated sites.
Quartz, citing TechCrunch, reported Color of Change's Nadine Smith said a blanket freeze is contested even among Democrats. Benzinga reported analyst Daniel Newman said demand would move abroad.
stories.sources_line: Sourced from CNBC (Democrats and data centers), Quartz, Benzinga, November 05, 2026.

stories.headline: Newsom Moves to Commute All 548 California Death Sentences
stories.dek: The outgoing governor announced the largest mass commutation in modern U.S. history, drawing praise from reform advocates and criticism from victims' groups.
pole_a_bullets: Voters kept the death penalty, and a governor should not nullify it unilaterally for the whole death row.
Victims' families say the move tells them the killers' lives matter more than their loved ones' lives.
Prosecutors and police argue sentences imposed by juries and courts should be carried out or left to the courts, not wiped away in one stroke.
Critics see a political motive, noting Newsom is outgoing and a potential 2028 presidential candidate.
pole_b_bullets: Newsom calls state-sanctioned killing incompatible with California's values and undermines the legal system.
The system is error-prone, and death sentences fall unevenly by race and county.
California has not executed anyone in 20 years, so the sentences were symbolic. Life without parole keeps these inmates imprisoned.
The order does not repeal the death penalty, and some cases still need California Supreme Court approval.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions commonly voiced by victims' rights groups, prosecutors, police and Republican officials.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions commonly voiced by death penalty opponents, reform advocates and Newsom.
evidence_left: The San Francisco Chronicle reported Newsom announced Thursday he will commute all 548 sentences to life without parole. The group includes 19 women and 529 men.
CBS Sacramento reported the move does not repeal the death penalty. Some cases need California Supreme Court review because of multiple-felony rules.
evidence_right: The Marshall Project reported the move would shrink the U.S. death row population by nearly a third, while The Washington Post reported about a quarter. It also reported criticism from victims' groups, prosecutors and police began last month.
Al Jazeera reported California has not executed a prisoner in 20 years. Newsom wrote that voters chose to keep the death penalty and he respects that.
stories.sources_line: Sourced from San Francisco Chronicle, The Marshall Project, The Washington Post, CBS Sacramento, November 05, 2026.

stories.headline: CVS Health to Split Into Two Companies, Reversing Its Aetna-Era Strategy
stories.dek: The company will separate Aetna and Caremark from its retail pharmacies, and shares fell more than 10% on the news.
pole_a_bullets: Each company gets a sharper strategy, its own capital structure and more agility.
The retail unit has returned to growth, so management argues it can split from strength rather than weakness.
Analysts cited by NBC viewed the split positively, and CVS raised its adjusted profit forecast to at least $8.20.
Shareholders receive stock in both companies in a tax-free transaction.
pole_b_bullets: The stock fell more than 10%, suggesting investors doubt the plan or its payoff.
The split reverses a decade-old integration strategy, and it is unclear how much of the commercial relationship between the units survives.
The retail unit still lags online rivals such as Amazon. One expert guessed a standalone pharmacy company may scrutinize and close weak stores.
Medical cost trends remain elevated, and the separation runs to 2028, leaving years of execution risk.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions commonly voiced by CVS management and some Wall Street analysts.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions commonly voiced by skeptical investors and healthcare industry analysts.
evidence_left: CVS confirmed the plan in a Nov. 4 release, as reported by Becker's: one company with Aetna, Caremark, Oak Street and Signify, and CVS Pharmacy with about 9,000 stores. Completion is expected in the first half of 2028, though CNN wrote early 2028.
The deal unwinds the 2018 Aetna acquisition, which CNN valued at $69 billion and Healthcare Dive described as a $78 billion merger.
evidence_right: NBC News reported shares fell more than 10% in early trading Wednesday. It also reported CVS raised its annual adjusted profit forecast to at least $8.20 while noting elevated medical cost trends.
NBC News reported the split follows growing scrutiny of vertically integrated healthcare firms, while CNBC reported CEO David Joyner said regulation was not the reason.
stories.sources_line: Sourced from NBC News, CNN, Healthcare Dive, Becker's Payer Issues, November 05, 2026.

stories.headline: LIV Golf to Wind Down After Failing to Secure Backing for 2.0 Relaunch
stories.dek: A LIV attorney told a bankruptcy court Thursday the Saudi-backed league will liquidate rather than relaunch in 2027.
pole_a_bullets: The numbers show a failed model: about $5 billion invested and about $3 billion in net operating losses.
Stars left before the end, including Koepka, Rahm, Reed and Garcia, which suggests players preferred the PGA Tour.
Weak sponsorship and U.S. TV audiences meant revenue never matched the spending.
The PGA Tour is vindicated, and the Tour is right not to extend its Returning Member Program to Rahm and DeChambeau.
pole_b_bullets: Fans did not kill LIV. Saudi PIF stopped funding in April and BC Partners withdrew its planned $300 million.
LIV changed golf's economics, with guaranteed contracts above $100 million that pushed pay across the sport.
Players are left in limbo, with unclear one-year Tour bans and contract claims such as Rahm's reported $100 million.
With the rival gone, the PGA Tour faces less competitive pressure, which could mean fewer options for players and fans.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions commonly voiced by PGA Tour-aligned commentators and golf columnists.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions commonly voiced by players' advocates and commentators who credit LIV with changing golf.
evidence_left: UPI reported court filings show PIF invested about $5 billion in LIV Golf, which had about $3 billion in net operating losses. The league filed for Chapter 11 on Sept. 8, per KRCR.
UPI reported Brooks Koepka, Jon Rahm, Patrick Reed and Sergio Garcia left over the past year. Golf Digest, via KIRO 7, reported only four players had said publicly they would return in 2027.
evidence_right: CBC reported PIF changed strategy and said it would stop paying for LIV after the 2026 season. CBS Sports reported BC Partners pulled its planned $300 million investment after the league failed to secure enough players.

KRCR reported Rahm agreed to give up claims reportedly worth about $100 million, and players who leave LIV face a one-year PGA Tour ban. It is unclear whether that can be reversed. CBC reported LIV paid $15.6 million to retain seven executives.
stories.sources_line: Sourced from ESPN, UPI, CBC Sports, CBS Sports, November 05, 2026.
